title: Luscious Gooey Middle Eastern Lamb Tagine
description: A rich and flavorful one-pot dish featuring tender lamb, tangy tamarind, and sweet nuka-pickle, perfect for a special occasion or a cozy night in.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large clay or ceramic tagine or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is softened and lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the lamb pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Add the tamarind pulp, nuka-pickle, cumin, coriander, and salt, and stir to combine.
Pour in 2 cups of water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the tagine, and simmer for 2 1/2 hours, or until the lamb is tender.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
Traditionally, the tagine is served with crusty bread or over couscous.
You can also serve it with a side of roasted vegetables or a simple green salad.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
